epics.name: Transcript Ingestion
epics.goal: Accept transcripts from paste, file upload, and live capture, normalising all sources to a common internal format.

stories.title: Paste transcript input
stories.iWant: to paste a raw transcript into a textarea in the popup
stories.soThat: I can process transcripts from Otter.ai, Zoom, or any external source
acceptanceCriteria: Popup exposes a textarea that accepts arbitrary length text
Pasted text is detected for 'Name: text' speaker prefix pattern
If no speaker pattern is detected, transcript is treated as unlabelled
Submit button becomes enabled when textarea is non-empty

stories.title: File upload for .txt / .vtt / .srt
stories.iWant: to upload a transcript file from my computer
stories.soThat: I can process downloaded Google Meet or Zoom transcript files
acceptanceCriteria: File input accepts .txt, .vtt, .srt extensions
File type is detected by extension and content sniff
Files over 10MB show a clear rejection message
Successfully parsed file populates the internal transcript buffer

stories.title: VTT parser
stories.iWant: a WebVTT state-machine parser
stories.soThat: VTT files become normalised transcript objects
acceptanceCriteria: WEBVTT header is skipped
Timestamp pairs (HH:MM:SS.mmm --> HH:MM:SS.mmm) are extracted
Speaker is inferred from 'Name: text' prefix inside cue text
Output is an array of {speaker, text, timestamp} objects

stories.title: SRT parser
stories.iWant: a SubRip parser
stories.soThat: SRT files become normalised transcript objects
acceptanceCriteria: Numbered cue blocks are parsed correctly
Comma-separated millisecond timestamps are handled
Speaker inference matches VTT parser behaviour
Output shape is identical to VTT parser output

stories.title: Plain text parser
stories.iWant: a plain-text normaliser
stories.soThat: unstructured transcripts still flow through the same pipeline
acceptanceCriteria: Detects 'Name: text' prefix on each line when present
Falls back to single unlabelled block when no pattern matches
Output shape matches VTT/SRT parsers

epics.name: Live Caption Capture
epics.goal: Capture live captions from Google Meet and Microsoft Teams via MutationObserver and persist per-tab.

stories.title: Google Meet caption content script
stories.iWant: the extension to capture live captions while I am in a Meet call
stories.soThat: I can process the meeting without downloading a transcript
acceptanceCriteria: Content script injects only on meet.google.com
MutationObserver watches caption container via structural selector / ARIA role (not class names)
Added nodes with non-empty textContent are buffered
Speaker label is extracted from sibling element when present
Buffer is persisted to chrome.storage.session keyed by tab id

stories.title: Microsoft Teams caption content script
stories.iWant: caption capture to also work on Teams
stories.soThat: my workflow is identical regardless of platform
acceptanceCriteria: Content script injects only on teams.microsoft.com
Teams-specific caption selector logic is isolated from Meet logic
Output buffer shape is identical to Meet capture

stories.title: Process current meeting button
stories.iWant: a single-click button to process whatever is buffered for the active tab
stories.soThat: I can generate notes the moment the meeting ends
acceptanceCriteria: Button reads buffer from chrome.storage.session for the active tab
Disabled state when buffer is empty
Clicking sends buffer through the same pipeline as paste/upload

epics.name: Claude Structured Extraction
epics.goal: Send normalised transcripts to Claude and receive structured JSON output; handle long meetings via multi-pass chunking.

stories.title: Claude API single-pass extraction
stories.iWant: short transcripts to be processed in a single Claude call
stories.soThat: I get results quickly when the meeting is under ~10 minutes
acceptanceCriteria: Background worker calls Claude with structured JSON output prompt
Response conforms to schema: action_items, decisions, open_questions, summary, attendees
Malformed responses surface a user-visible error
API key is read from extension settings, never hard-coded

stories.title: Multi-pass chunking for long meetings
stories.iWant: 2-hour transcripts to be processed accurately
stories.soThat: nothing important is lost to truncation
acceptanceCriteria: Transcripts over a word threshold are split into ~10-minute windows
Pass 1 extracts raw facts per chunk as JSON arrays
Pass 2 synthesises combined facts into final structured output
Total of two API calls for multi-pass (not one-per-chunk+synthesis)
Progress indicator shows 'Extracting facts...' then 'Synthesising output...'

stories.title: Speaker diarisation cleanup
stories.iWant: consecutive lines from the same speaker collapsed
stories.soThat: Claude sees clean dialogue and not fragmented captions
acceptanceCriteria: Adjacent entries with identical speaker are merged
Timestamps on merged entries retain earliest start
Unlabelled blocks are left untouched

epics.name: Tabbed Results UI
epics.goal: Display structured output in the popup across dedicated tabs.

stories.title: Popup shell with tabs
stories.iWant: separate tabs for Action Items, Decisions, Open Questions, Summary, Attendee Map
stories.soThat: I can focus on one output at a time
acceptanceCriteria: Five tabs render in the popup
Keyboard navigation between tabs works
Empty states are shown per tab when a section has no content

stories.title: Action Items view
stories.iWant: to see tasks with owner, due date, and priority
stories.soThat: I can triage follow-ups at a glance
acceptanceCriteria: Each item shows task, owner (or 'Unassigned'), due (or 'No date'), priority badge
Priority badge colour differs for high / medium / low
Checkbox renders next to each item for export

stories.title: Decisions / Open Questions / Summary views
stories.iWant: clean rendering of the three textual outputs
stories.soThat: they read well before exporting
acceptanceCriteria: Decisions display statement and attribution when present
Open Questions render as a bullet list
Summary renders as a single paragraph

stories.title: Attendee Map view
stories.iWant: to see who spoke, how much, and what topics they owned
stories.soThat: I can assess participation quickly
acceptanceCriteria: Renders attendees with topics and word count
Hidden when transcript has no speaker labels
Word count shown as a proportional bar

epics.name: Export Formats
epics.goal: Produce copy-ready output for Notion, Confluence, Slack, and plain email.

stories.title: Notion export
stories.iWant: to copy output as Notion-compatible markdown
stories.soThat: pasting into Notion produces native to-do blocks
acceptanceCriteria: Action items render as '- [ ] task' checkboxes
Headers use '# / ## / ###' consistent with Notion paste behaviour
Copy confirmation toast appears on success

stories.title: Confluence export
stories.iWant: Confluence wiki markup output
stories.soThat: I can paste directly into a Confluence page
acceptanceCriteria: Headers use h1./h2./h3. syntax
Action items render as Confluence task-list markup
Bullet lists use '*' with correct nesting

stories.title: Slack export
stories.iWant: Slack-formatted message output
stories.soThat: I can drop it straight into a channel
acceptanceCriteria: Headers use *bold* formatting
Bullet lists use '•' characters
Output is under Slack's message length limit or split with a notice

stories.title: Plain email export
stories.iWant: a professional meeting-notes email body
stories.soThat: I can forward it with minimal editing
acceptanceCriteria: Output is plain text with clear section headers
Includes suggested subject line derived from the summary
No markdown artefacts leak into the output

epics.name: Cross-Browser Packaging
epics.goal: Ship a working extension in Chrome, Edge, and Firefox.

stories.title: Chrome / Edge MV3 manifest
stories.iWant: an MV3 manifest with the right permissions
stories.soThat: the extension loads in Chromium browsers
acceptanceCriteria: Manifest declares content scripts for Meet and Teams domains
storage and activeTab permissions are declared
Service worker is registered as background

stories.title: Firefox compatibility
stories.iWant: the extension to run on Firefox
stories.soThat: Firefox users are supported
acceptanceCriteria: browser.* / chrome.* API differences are abstracted via a polyfill
Manifest passes web-ext lint
Loads in Firefox via about:debugging with full feature parity

stories.title: Settings popup
stories.iWant: a settings screen
stories.soThat: I can configure my Claude API key and default export format
acceptanceCriteria: API key input is masked by default
Key is stored in chrome.storage.local, never chrome.storage.sync
Default export format selector persists across sessions
